questions.q: A goods vehicle has a gross vehicle weight of 8,000 kg. Which licence is needed to drive it?
questions.explain: A C1 licence is for a goods vehicle whose gross vehicle weight is {{fact:licence.c1.weight_range}} (reg. 181).

questions.q: What is the maximum speed for a commercial vehicle whose gross vehicle weight exceeds {{fact:speed.heavy_threshold}}, on a non-urban road — including a freeway?
questions.explain: A commercial vehicle over {{fact:speed.heavy_threshold}} is limited to {{fact:speed.heavy.nonurban}} on any non-urban road, even on a freeway and even if a sign allows more (reg. 54).

questions.q: What determines which licence class is required for a goods vehicle?
options: The number of doors in the cab
The colour of the number plate alone
The colour of the vehicle and the type of load it carries
questions.explain: The licence class (C1/C/C+E) is derived from the vehicle's gross vehicle weight, not from its outward size or colour.

questions.q: What is the maximum overall width permitted for a vehicle, including its load?
questions.explain: The overall width of a vehicle, including its load, must not exceed {{fact:vehicle.width.max_m}} (reg. 313).

questions.q: What happens to the spring brake in a heavy vehicle when the air pressure drops?
options: It disconnects completely from the system
It closes on its own and stops the vehicle
It stays open and the vehicle keeps driving as normal
It has no connection to air pressure
questions.explain: The spring brake is held open by air pressure; when the pressure drops, the spring closes it on its own — a fail-safe, not a fault.

questions.q: Why does a heavy-vehicle driver use a retarder or an engine brake on a long descent?
options: To accelerate faster on the descent
Because using the foot brake on a descent is forbidden altogether
To slow down without heating and wearing the friction brakes
questions.explain: Repeated use of the friction brakes on a long descent heats them up to brake fade. A retarder and an engine brake slow the vehicle without wearing them.

questions.q: What must you make sure of before setting off in a vehicle with air brakes?
options: That there is a continuous air-leak sound from the tanks
That the throttle is stuck open
That the air pressure has risen to normal and the pressure warning has gone off
That the parking brake is fully released without checking the pressure
questions.explain: Driving with the air-pressure warning lit is dangerous and forbidden; you must make sure the pressure rises normally and there are no audible leaks.

questions.q: What braking system is common in trucks and buses, instead of hydraulic pressure?
questions.explain: A heavy vehicle commonly has an air brake system: a compressor compresses air into tanks, and pressing the pedal releases it into the brake chambers.

questions.q: Why is it especially dangerous to stand on the right side of a truck at a junction?
options: Because standing there is forbidden under the parking law
Because it is an area the driver cannot see, especially when the truck may turn right
Because that is where the truck is hottest, from the engine
Because that is where the vehicle is loudest
questions.explain: Even with all the mirrors, an area next to the front and the right side remains that the driver cannot see — especially dangerous when the truck is about to turn right.

questions.q: What is the phenomenon in which the rear wheels of a long vehicle pass closer to the corner than the front wheels in a turn?
questions.explain: Off-tracking is the more inward path that the rear wheels take in a turn, which grows with the length of the vehicle.

questions.q: On which vehicles is an extra convex mirror fitted on the right side, in addition to the two ordinary rear-view mirrors?
options: A goods vehicle and a work vehicle with a gross vehicle weight of {{fact:speed.heavy_threshold}} or more
questions.explain: A heavy goods vehicle and work vehicle have an extra convex mirror fitted on the right side, showing the area next to the front and side of the vehicle (reg. 361).

questions.q: A truck is about to turn left at a junction and looks as if it is edging slightly into the opposite lane before the turn. What is the right thing to do?
options: Hoot the horn so it hurries up
Rush to fill the gap it is leaving in the opposite lane
Overtake it on the left at that moment
Stay back and give it room — the gap is reserved for its tail
questions.explain: A long vehicle sometimes swings out towards the opposite side before a turn to leave room for the off-tracking of its rear wheels — the gap is not really free.

questions.q: How far may a load overhang beyond the vehicle's extreme front or rear point, with no special requirements?
questions.explain: An overhang of up to {{fact:load.overhang.front_rear_max_m}} beyond the vehicle's extreme point is permitted (reg. 85(a)(1)(b)).

questions.q: Above what load width is a “Caution – wide load” sign and perimeter lighting required?
questions.explain: On a heavy commercial vehicle, above a load width of {{fact:load.wide.sign_required_over_m}} a sign and perimeter lighting are required (reg. 85(c)).

questions.q: Above what load width are both an escort vehicle and a police-officer permit required?
questions.explain: Above a load width of {{fact:load.wide.escort_and_permit_over_m}}, both an escort vehicle and a permit from a police officer are required (reg. 85(c)).

questions.q: What is the legal consequence of carrying a load that is not secured as required by the load-securing standard?
options: A fixed fine only, with no points
No consequence as long as the load has not actually fallen
questions.explain: Carrying a load that is not secured as required is a court-summons offence carrying {{points:cargo-unsecured}} points (reg. 85(a)(4)).

questions.q: What is the difference between a “vehicle with a trailer attached” and a “combination vehicle”?
options: There is no difference, they are two names for the same thing
A vehicle with a trailer attached is always heavier than a combination vehicle
In a vehicle with a trailer attached, the trailer rests on its own wheels; in a combination vehicle, the semi-trailer rests on the towing unit
A combination vehicle is only a bus
questions.explain: A vehicle with a trailer attached = a motor vehicle with a trailer on its own wheels. A combination vehicle = a towing unit that a semi-trailer rests on at its front, with no front wheels of its own (reg. 1).

questions.q: What are the two parts that connect the tractor unit to the semi-trailer?
options: A warning triangle and a reflector
A speed limiter and a tachograph
A fifth wheel (coupling plate) and a kingpin
A convex mirror and a rear light
questions.explain: The fifth wheel on the tractor unit and a kingpin projecting from the bottom of the semi-trailer lock into each other and let the combination vehicle turn.

questions.q: The semi-trailer starts to slide sideways and fold relative to the tractor unit. What is the correct response?
options: Ease off the brake slightly and correct the steering gently
Open the cab door and jump out
questions.explain: Braking harder worsens jackknifing. The correct response is to ease off the brake slightly and correct the steering gently.

questions.q: What are the conditions for obtaining a C+E licence?
options: Age 17 only, with no prior seniority
10 years' seniority in any vehicle licence
Age {{fact:licence.ce.min_age}} and at least {{fact:licence.ce.seniority_c}} year's seniority in a C licence
Any holder of a B licence can get it immediately
questions.explain: A C+E licence requires age {{fact:licence.ce.min_age}} and at least {{fact:licence.ce.seniority_c}} year's seniority in a C licence (reg. 189).

questions.q: How long may a public-vehicle or heavy-goods-vehicle driver drive continuously without a break of at least an hour?
options: No limit as long as there is fuel
questions.explain: You must not drive more than {{fact:hours.continuous-cap}} continuously without a break of at least an hour (reg. 168).

questions.q: What is the maximum driving permitted for a public-vehicle or heavy-goods-vehicle driver in any 24-hour period, and how much in a week?
options: No daily limit, only a weekly one
8 hours in 24 hours, 40 hours in a week
questions.explain: The limit is up to {{fact:hours.daily.max}} in 24 hours and up to {{fact:hours.weekly.max}} in any 7-day period (reg. 168).

questions.q: What does the tachograph record in a vehicle subject to the driving-hours regulation?
options: Only the amount of fuel consumed
Only the number of passengers in the vehicle
Driving speed, distance, and the driver's driving and rest times
questions.explain: The tachograph continuously records speed, distance, and driving and rest times, for monitoring fatigue and working hours (reg. 364D).

questions.q: What is the legal position on driving a heavy commercial vehicle without a working tachograph?
options: It is permitted only on a short urban trip
A verbal warning only, with no fine
It is permitted, as long as the driver knows how many hours they have driven
questions.explain: Driving without a working tachograph is a fixed-fine offence of {{fine:tachograph-faulty}} and {{points:tachograph-faulty}} points (reg. 364D).

questions.q: What is the maximum speed of a tractor and a mobile machine, and what is their status on a freeway?
options: {{fact:speed.urban}}, allowed on a freeway with care
{{fact:speed.slow_vehicle}}, and a freeway is completely closed to them
There is no speed limit for a tractor
questions.explain: A tractor and a mobile machine are limited to {{fact:speed.slow_vehicle}} on any road, and a freeway is closed to them (reg. 54).

questions.q: What is the minimum age for a class 1 (tractor) licence?
questions.explain: A class 1 licence is given from age {{fact:licence.tractor.min_age}} (reg. 188).

questions.q: What is the maximum gross vehicle weight of a trailer that a tractor on a class 1 licence may tow?
questions.explain: A tractor on a class 1 licence may tow a trailer with a gross vehicle weight of up to {{fact:licence.tractor.trailer_max}} (reg. 179).
